output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against one of the 13 who never worked on it. That makes a group-wide pay gap, the firm-wide hours increase and ordinary market movement unlikely main causes. Those would hit all 24 associates, not mainly the Kestrel team. Pay may still play a minor role, but I found no evidence that it is the driver.

I cannot yet say whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the way Dorian Faulk supervises. All 11 Kestrel associates report to him, and he supervises no one else, so the records can't separate the two. The survey points at both: unsustainable workload and disrespectful treatment. I am moderately sure about the concentration and not sure about which of the two causes it is.

Next steps:
- Do not announce the £12k payment or close the review. It would cost £228k, miss the concentrated problem and end the inquiry.
- Commission the confidential external interviews (about £9k, within three weeks), designed to separate supervision from workload.
- Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting.
- Hold the supervision change and contract reviewers until the interviews report. Kestrel moves to four associates in January 2027, so the interviews should finish before then.
